readings: Join Laboratory to Patient on ID. For each SEX value, compute the average of CPK/GPT (real-valued division) over its lab tests, skipping tests where the ratio is NULL, for example when GPT is NULL or 0. Let M1 be the unweighted mean of these per-sex averages. Keep the sexes whose average is above M1. Let M2 be the unweighted mean of the kept sexes' averages. Keep only the kept sexes whose average is strictly above M2. In one row with no rounding, return the average of the remaining sexes' averages, the average of (their average − M1), and the average of (their average − M2).

Join Laboratory to Patient on ID. For each SEX value, compute the average of CPK/GPT (real-valued division) over its lab tests, skipping tests where the ratio is NULL, for example when GPT is NULL or 0. Let M1 be the unweighted mean of these per-sex averages. Keep the sexes whose average is above M1. Let M2 be the pooled mean of the individual test-level CPK/GPT ratios across all tests belonging to the kept sexes. Keep only the kept sexes whose average is strictly above M2. In one row with no rounding, return the average of the remaining sexes' averages, the average of (their average − M1), and the average of (their average − M2).
queries:
WITH s AS (
  SELECT P.SEX AS sex, AVG(CAST(L.CPK AS REAL) / L.GPT) AS a
  FROM Laboratory L
  JOIN Patient P ON L.ID = P.ID
  WHERE L.GPT IS NOT NULL AND L.GPT <> 0 AND L.CPK IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY P.SEX
),
m1 AS (SELECT AVG(a) AS v FROM s),
k1 AS (SELECT s.sex, s.a FROM s, m1 WHERE s.a > m1.v),
m2 AS (SELECT AVG(a) AS v FROM k1),
k2 AS (SELECT k1.sex, k1.a FROM k1, m2 WHERE k1.a > m2.v)
SELECT AVG(k2.a) AS avg_a,
       AVG(k2.a - m1.v) AS avg_diff_m1,
       AVG(k2.a - m2.v) AS avg_diff_m2
FROM k2, m1, m2;
WITH t AS (
  SELECT P.SEX AS SEX, CAST(L.CPK AS REAL) / L.GPT AS r
  FROM Laboratory L
  JOIN Patient P ON L.ID = P.ID
  WHERE L.GPT IS NOT NULL AND L.GPT != 0 AND L.CPK IS NOT NULL
),
s AS (
  SELECT SEX, AVG(r) AS a FROM t GROUP BY SEX
),
m1 AS (
  SELECT AVG(a) AS v FROM s
),
k1 AS (
  SELECT s.SEX, s.a FROM s, m1 WHERE s.a > m1.v
),
m2 AS (
  SELECT AVG(r) AS v FROM t WHERE SEX IN (SELECT SEX FROM k1)
),
k2 AS (
  SELECT k1.SEX, k1.a FROM k1, m2 WHERE k1.a > m2.v
)
SELECT AVG(k2.a) AS avg_a,
       AVG(k2.a - m1.v) AS avg_a_minus_m1,
       AVG(k2.a - m2.v) AS avg_a_minus_m2
FROM k2, m1, m2;
